supersedes: RECEIPT-o7.json revision 2 (WITHDRAWN) and the three per-cell receipts marked withdrawn

why_rebuilt: the trees and the third-party tools had been built on the host against a newer glibc and do not run in the court (`GLIBC_2.38`/`GLIBC_2.42` not found, `libcrypt.so.2` missing)
so build_trees.sh and build_tools.sh were re-run inside the court; both exit 0
court_environment_requirements: a subreaper: PID 1 in the container does not reap orphans, so ssh-agent becomes a zombie and `kill -0` stops t-exec advancing past agent-subprocess
the authority `openssl` CLI on PATH (ssh2putty.sh calls it)
venue.untracked_helpers: court/tmp/o4/{subreaper,openssl shim} - venue aids, not test changes

hypothesis_tested: the BA/AB host-key mismatch seen in the host venue was a stale copied regress .ssh/known_hosts, not a cross-library difference
hypothesis_result: confirmed: with the copied known_hosts removed, no host-key mismatch occurs in any cell, and no dropbear ciphers failure occurs either

result.classification: upstream-common and unsupported, not candidate-specific: dbclient's own transcript says `No matching algo kex` (Dropbear 2026.94 does not offer diffie-hellman-group14-sha1, which dropbear-kex.sh forces on the server)

hazard_recorded.what: `t-exec` iterates `$?` - the prerequisites newer than the target - so the set of scripts it runs depends on file mtimes
hazard_recorded.evidence: the same tree and the same make target ran 73 scripts on the host and 96 in the court, where the tree had just been extracted and built
hazard_recorded.consequence: the two venues' counts are not comparable, and a run can silently cover fewer scripts than intended
hazard_recorded.fix_pending: touch regress/*.sh before the run so the selection is maximal and deterministic; not yet in cell.sh
